title: Add compact sanity digest and perf snapshot embeds
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: onboarding new model variants currently triggers large, slow changelog generation and heavyweight perf profile runs. For small rollouts and automated pre-flight checks we need a compact, deterministic sanity artifact that: 1) captures a tiny set of representative prompts and gold answers for quality smoke-tests; 2) includes a lightweight performance snapshot (latency histogram + few key stats) encoded as an embedding so changelog automation can diff and surface regressions without re-running full suites. This PR introduces two pieces: (a) a compact sanity digest format (JSON + metadata) produced at model intake and stored alongside profile artifacts, and (b) perf-snapshot-embeds: a normalized vector representation of a perf histogram and 3 summary stats used by release note generation to compute significance and show human-friendly deltas.

What changed:
- New generator: scripts/generate_sanity_digest.py — CLI that consumes a model package (or local model weights) and a small promptset to output a stamped digest with deterministic ordering, sample ids, and tokenized signatures. The script has smoke-test and CI modes.
- Registry integration: pkg/onboard/digest.go — lightweight producer/consumer for digest artifacts and an upload flow to the model registry. Adds UploadSanityDigest and VerifyDigest APIs used by onboarding pipeline.
- Perf embedding: tooling in pkg/onboard/perf_embed.go and a small Go port of the embedding normalization used by Optimize team. The embedter converts latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) + error-rate into a 64-d float32 vector which is then base64-encoded for storage in the manifest.
- Changelog hook: tools/changelog/snapshot-diff-annotator.py — uses the perf snapshot embeds to compute cosine-distance deltas and render short humanized lines in the generated release note (e.g., "perf: p95 latency +8% (small regression) — see perf-snapshot-diff").
- Docs & CI: docs/sanity-digest.md documents the format and intended usage; ci/regression-check.yml adds an optional sanity-digest check step that fails CI only in strict mode.

Motivation and trade-offs: the digest is intentionally tiny (<= 8 samples) to be inexpensive and deterministic across environments and quantization modes; it isn't a replacement for full perf or eval runs. The perf-embed is designed to be robust to sample noise and to surface actionable deltas to humans and downstream automation.

Backwards compatibility: existing onboarding flows that don't produce the digest are unaffected; changelog annotator gracefully skips absent artifacts.

Testing: unit tests for serialization, round-trip verification, and an integration test that simulates registry upload and changelog diff.

Rollout plan: produce digests for the next two model intake jobs and enable changelog annotations for canary release notes.

Related Linear items: ENG-6231 (digest schema), ENG-6269 (perf embedter), PM-88 (changelog UX).
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial python digest producer; go registry integration and API hooks; perf-embed implementation and tests; docs and CI. Key commits: 'add python sanity digest generator', 'introduce UploadSanityDigest/VerifyDigest API', 'perf embedding algorithm and unit tests', 'changelog annotator and docs'.
ci_checks_summary: CI initially failed on lint for python script (flake8 errors) and a flaky integration test (timing). Lint fixes and a test timeout increase were pushed in second commit. All checks passing on rerun: unit, integration, linters, go vet, build. Optional CI step 'sanity-digest-check' is allowed to be non-blocking unless the 'strict-digest' label is set.
review_comments: Diego Rivera: Nice compact format. Suggest including tokenized length in the digest header to help quantization-aware verification. -- addressed in digest.go (added TokenCount).

Ava Patel: Can we guarantee determinism across CPU/GPU and quantized builds? How do we ensure sample ordering? -- replied: script sorts samples by stable id and uses explicit RNG seed; unit test added to verify byte-for-byte for same inputs.
Jonah Lee: The perf-embed dimensions look arbitrary; please add comments and a short doc explaining normalization choices. -- addressed in perf_embed.go and docs/sanity-digest.md with math appendix.
release_notes:
- introduce compact sanity digest (<=8 canonical samples) to surface quick quality smoke-tests for new model variants.
- add perf-snapshot-embeds and changelog annotator to surface concise perf deltas in autogenerated release notes.
- tooling: generator script, registry upload hooks, and CI optional checks.
